body:
# Reuse the boxed server.port endpoint tag

Reuse the boxed `server.port` value for metrics and traces.

## Description

Reuse the boxed `server.port` value in the connection endpoint tags instead of boxing the local port on every call. The local port is almost always one of the few ports the server listens on, so the first boxed value is cached and never replaced. Other ports are boxed as before.

Because the cache is never overwritten, the field is only read after startup, so a server with traffic on more than one listener doesn't contend on it between cores. Replacing the most recently boxed value instead made a changing port 2-5x slower than boxing under concurrency (see below).

The tags are added twice per HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 stream when `kestrel.queued_requests` is enabled, and once per SignalR hub invocation activity.

### Benchmarks

#### `KestrelMetricsBenchmark.QueuedRequest`

`kestrel.queued_requests` start and stop for one HTTP/2 stream with a listener attached. `Ports=2` alternates the local port between streams. Medians of 4 interleaved rounds.

| Ports | main | Replace last boxed | First boxed (this PR) | Allocated (main / replace / first) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 98.4 ns | 83.7 ns (−15%) | 80.7 ns (−18%) | 48 B / 0 B / 0 B |
| 2 | 95.4 ns | 98.1 ns (+3%) | 93.2 ns (−2%) | 48 B / 24 B / 24 B |

#### Cache on its own, 12 concurrent threads

Time per call on each thread. Allocations are the total across threads.

| Local port | Box every time | Replace last boxed | First boxed (this PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Same on every call | 18.9 ns, 288 B | 6.4 ns, 0 B | 6.5 ns, 0 B |
| Alternates every call | 18.4 ns, 288 B | 98.3 ns, 287 B | 13.0 ns, 144 B |
| Fixed per thread, differs between threads | 18.5 ns, 288 B | 41.9 ns, 18 B | 17.7 ns, 264 B |

On a single thread, a hit takes 1.4 ns versus 2.6 ns to box, and a miss takes 2.5 ns.

#### `DefaultHubDispatcherTelemetryBenchmark.Invocation`

The benchmark (reused from #69557) now has a `Ports` parameter. With tracing, a stable port saves 24 B per invocation (2,064 B → 2,040 B). Run-to-run noise (±30-70 ns on ~650 ns) is too large to resolve the time difference.

<details>

<summary>Environment</summary>

``` ini
BenchmarkDotNet=v0.13.0, OS=Windows 10.0.26300
Intel Core i7-13700H, pinned to the P-cores
.NET 12.0.0-alpha.1.26521.103 (in-repo, InProcessEmitToolchain)
.NET 11.0 RC 3 (standalone cache benchmark, BenchmarkDotNet 0.16.0-preview.2, workstation GC)
```

</details>

commits.messageBody:
Replacing the cached boxed port on every miss writes a shared static from
the hot path. When a server has traffic on more than one listener, the
cache line bounces between cores and the cache is 2-5x slower than boxing.

Cache the first port seen and never replace it, so the field is only read
after startup. Other ports are boxed as before.

Add a Kestrel kestrel.queued_requests benchmark and a Ports parameter to
the SignalR telemetry benchmark to measure a changing local port.

Assisted-by: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Only cache the first boxed server.port value
